title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding progress, environment access, and initial inference results. Customer still working through VPC peering and KMS key access; SE validated a small benchmark run and identified tokenization mismatch and batching misconfig in one route. Next steps: Redwood to share tuned inference config and benchmark spreadsheet; customer to provide KMS ARN and complete VPC peering by next week; schedule deep dive on security with Laura and Redwood security doc walkthrough.
topics: Onboarding: account roles, API keys, routes
action_items: Mark R: finish VPC peering test and confirm security group rules by 2027-04-26
MedSync: provide KMS ARN and service account details by 2027-04-26
Jordan L: send tuned inference config and benchmark spreadsheet (including tokenization checks) by 2027-04-23
Ravi P: schedule security deep-dive with Laura and share SOC2/ISO checklist by 2027-04-28
Priya S: re-run sample inference with updated tokenizer and share logs by 2027-04-24
next_steps: Redwood to upload tuned config + benchmark results to shared drive
Customer to complete VPC peering and confirm KMS access
Schedule security deep dive next Tue or Wed
Demo of canary rollout + auto-fallback on next sync if env is ready
header:
Date: 2027-04-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Mina Torres (Redwood CSM), Alicia Gomez (CTO - MedSync), Mark Reynolds (SRE), Priya Shah (ML Engineer), Samir Desai (Product), Laura Chen (Security)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, and we have Ravi and Mina with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alicia Gomez: Good, thanks. Busy week but ready to go.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda — quick access updates, go over the small benchmark results Ravi ran, discuss tuning suggestions and surface any blockers.
[00:22] Mark Reynolds: Sounds good. For access, we're stuck on V P C peering, the cloud team needs the exact CIDR and one more security group rule, I think.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Right, Mark — sorry, CIDR is 10.48.0.0/16 from our side, and we need the inbound on 9090 tcp for the placement agent, plus the NFS mount for logs — I mentioned in the doc. Also we need the K M S ARN so we can validate key policies.
[00:45] Mark Reynolds: Yeah, we saw that doc, I think Laura has the K M S request in flight. Laura, any update?
[00:50] Laura Chen: I put the K M S request through, but the ARN hasn't been approved by compliance yet. There's a question about key rotation and H S M vs managed keys.
[01:00] Mina Torres: We can support both — for the pilot we often use a customer-managed K M S ARN; our Private deployment also supports H S M if needed. For the POC, the main ask is just that we can decrypt the model artifacts.
[01:15] Alicia Gomez: Ok that helps.
[01:18] Ravi Patel: On the benchmark — quick recap: we ran the sample inference suite you provided (Priya's three prompts set), 100 inferences each, two models: base-open-6b and a quantized 6b variant. We measured median latency and p95. Median for base-open-6b was 210 ms, p95 610 ms. For quantized variant median 260 ms, p95 740 ms. But we saw a tokenization mismatch on prompt set B that inflated token counts.
[01:45] Priya Shah: Right — I noticed that in our logs — tokens reported by Redwood were ~1.4x compared to our local tokenizer for certain unicode sequences.
[01:55] Ravi Patel: Yeah, could be a mismatch in the tokenizer model or an input normalization step. We suspect the infer server is using a different token table — sometimes the model vetting step picks a compatible tokenizer fallback. We can force the same tokenizer during preprocessing.
[02:10] Priya Shah: Ok, we'll re-run with the exact tokenizer artifact attached — I'll upload the tokenizer.json to the shared folder.
[02:16] Jordan Lee: Great. Also noticed in traces that one route had low batching — route /generate-news had concurrency 1 which increased overhead. For latency-sensitive routes you can increase batch size and reduce max latency; we recommended continuous batching config in the doc.
[02:30] Samir Desai: Wait — but won't increasing batch size hurt latency for interactive flows? Our product needs sub-300 ms median.
[02:37] Ravi Patel: It's a tradeoff — for short prompts small batch sizes help, but we use dynamic batching heuristics: set max_batch_size to 8 and max_wait_ms to 20ms as starting point, plus prefix KV caching for repeated prefixes. That kept median within 240 ms in our internal tests.
[02:55] Mark Reynolds: Were the runs on Dedicated or Hosted? We are concerned about noisy neighbors.
[03:00] Ravi Patel: These were on a small Dedicated pool we spun up for the POC — 2 x A100-sim nodes. We can reproduce similar numbers on Hosted but compute isolation is better on Dedicated.
[03:12] Laura Chen: Security question — do you keep audit logs for inference requests and do you redact P I I at rest? We need retention policy info.
[03:20] Mina Torres: We keep audit logs and can align retention windows. For Hosted we offer configurable retention, and for Private you control log storage. We do have redaction helpers but recommend customers not send raw P I I. We'll share the security pack with SOC2 sections.
[03:35] Alicia Gomez: Good. Also timeline check — goal is to have pilot validating latency & cost targets by end of next week. Is that still realistic?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: If V P C peering and K M S are done by Tuesday, yes. Biggest blocker is access.
[03:50] Mark Reynolds: We'll prioritize.
[03:52] Priya Shah: Quick question on model rollout — can you do canary and automatic fallback?
[03:58] Ravi Patel: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. We can set traffic weights and a health check that monitors latency and error rate and fallback to a cheaper variant if thresholds breach. We'll demo that next week if environment is ready.
[04:12] Priya Shah: Awesome. Also about tokenization — will you accept our tokenizer artifact or do we need to convert it?
[04:18] Ravi Patel: We accept tokenizer.json and token-merges files; just zip and upload. If there are unicode normalisations we'll run a preproc step.
[04:26] Priya Shah: Ok I'll upload now.
[04:29] (short pause, sounds of typing)
[04:34] Mark Reynolds: One more infra thing — we are going to want metrics exported to our Prometheus. How does Redwood integrate?
[04:40] Jordan Lee: We expose metrics via a Prom endpoint for Private/Dedicated; Hosted can push via remote write to your ingest. We'll share a sample config.
[04:48] Mark Reynolds: Perfect.
[04:50] Samir Desai: On cost — any initial numbers on cost per 1k tokens? We need rough unit economics to compare to Anthropic.
[04:58] Ravi Patel: For the pilot config with quantized variant we're seeing ~ $0.15 per 1k tokens at our test batch sizes; base-open-6b was ~ $0.22 per 1k. These are estimates; we'll send a detailed benchmark with token counts and runtime.
[05:15] Alicia Gomez: Sounds reasonable.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: Quick recap: Mark to finish V P C peering and confirm SGs; Laura to finalise K M S approval; Priya to upload tokenizer artifact and re-run sample; Redwood to send tuned config and benchmark spreadsheet and schedule security deep-dive.
[05:30] Laura Chen: Can we get a security doc link in chat?
[05:33] Mina Torres: Yes, I'll post the SOC2/ISO checklist and the private deployment security whitepaper to the shared folder after the call.
[05:41] Priya Shah: One small note — logs from last run show an error 502 for 3 requests around 14:12, do you want logs?
[05:48] Ravi Patel: Yes please send the logs, include request ids, we'll triage. Could be transient placement or burst.
[05:54] Priya Shah: Will do.
[05:56] Jordan Lee: Ok, any other questions?
[06:00] Samir Desai: Nothing from product.
[06:03] Alicia Gomez: No, thanks everyone.
[06:06] Jordan Lee: Thanks — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and configs today. Talk next week. Bye.
[06:12] (call ends)
references: Spreadsheet: initial-benchmark-2027-04-21.xlsx (to be uploaded by Jordan)
